title.value: Synthetic Routes to Allenic Acids and Esters and Their Stereospecific Conversion to Butenolides

abstract.value: The synthesis of allenic acids and esters and their conversion to butenolides has been examined in some detail. Racemic butenolides 10 are efficiently prepared from the esters 8 through treatment with $\mathbf { B C l _ { 3 } }$ and exposure of the derived acid 9 to catalytic ${ \bf A g N O _ { 3 } }$ in acetone. Conversion of the enantioenriched allenylstannane (S)-17 to the acid 18 through lithiation and subsequent carboxylation with $\mathbf { C O _ { 2 } }$ afforded racemic product. The enantioenriched propargylic mesylates 16 and 22 afforded the allenic esters 19 and 23 with inversion of configuration through treatment with $\mathrm { P d } ( \mathrm { P h } _ { 3 } \mathrm { P } ) _ { 4 }$, CO, and the appropriate alcohol in THF. These reactions proceeded with ca. 10% or less of racemization. The allenic esters 23 yielded the iodobutenolides 24 by reaction with IBr. Hydrogenolysis to the butenolide 25 was achieved with Pd(PPh<sub>3</sub>)<sub>4</sub> and $\mathbf { B u _ { 3 } S n H }.$. Alternatively, the allenic acids 27 could be prepared directly from mesylates 22 with $\mathbf { P d } ( \mathbf { P P h } _ { 3 } ) _ { 4 }$ and CO in aqueous THF. Cyclization to the butenolides 25 was achieved, as before, with catalytic ${ \bf A g N O _ { 3 } }$
